reviewer: /root main coordinator; source-level review; tests not executed
title: Cashier Operations and Control Center safe-drop recovery divergence
scope: Compare two active Cashier WinUI entry points for the same SafeDropRequest/server operation, including request validation, approval, shift/business-day gates, uncertainty/replay, persistence, and test coverage. Supplement to SEM-028 and UI-001.
decision: BOTH VIEWS POST THE SAME SAFE-DROP COMMAND AND SERVER ENFORCES THE SAME MONEY RULES. CONTROL CENTER USES A DURABLE OWNER-KEYED RETAINED REQUEST; CASHIER OPERATIONS RETAINS ONLY IN MEMORY. THIS IS A SOURCE-CONFIRMED CLIENT RECOVERY DIVERGENCE UNDER PROCESS LOSS, NOT PROOF OF A DUPLICATE MOVEMENT. REUSE UI-001; NO NEW FINDING ID.

behavior.shared: Both surfaces use SafeDropRequest, SafeDropAsync and SafeDropHandler. The server owns amount/permission/day/shift/balance validation and transactional Drawer-to-Main posting. Their business context gates differ: cashier flow is shift/operation oriented; Control Center requires an active business day and open shift for new safe-drop entry. This distinction is consistent with their surrounding screens and was not treated as an error.
behavior.cashier_operations: CashierViewModel.Operations keeps `_pendingSafeDrop` and `_SafeDropRequestId` in the current view model. It blocks cancel/edit while pending and retries the exact request in-process; AppSession pending state is also process-only. No durable owner-keyed RetainedRequest is used by this entry point.
behavior.control_center: ControlCenterViewModel.Reconciliation uses RetainedRequest<SafeDropRequest> with stable owner key `controlcenter.safe-drop`; constructor restores pending request from the configured cashier FileRetainedRequestStore and exposes unresolved state. RetainedRequestStore Save catches errors and continues; App config supplies no callback, so durable-save failure is a residual best-effort limitation.

cross_file_call_chain: ControlCenterViewModel.Reconciliation.SubmitSafeDropAsync -> RetainedRequest.SendAsync -> FileRetainedRequestStore.Save before POST (best effort) -> ApiClient.SafeDropAsync -> same SafeDropHandler; constructor reloads request from stable owner key.
AppSession protects cashier flow navigation only while current process state exists; the Control Center retained DTO is process-persistent when local store save/load succeeds.

existing_finding.relationship: UI-001 already identifies process-loss recovery gaps and its prior challenge explicitly requested independent safe-drop path evidence. This comparison supplies that evidence and expands the existing finding record only; no duplicate finding.

counterevidence_and_limits: Both flows preserve exact ID/payload during same-process retry.
Control Center improves process-restart recovery when local storage succeeds.

FileRetainedRequestStore catches disk errors; because no callback is supplied at app bootstrap, the current request can still be sent even if persistence failed. This is a conditional storage failure limitation, not a reproduced incident.
Existing CloseoutRegression test verifies only in-memory identical retry, not app/view-model reconstruction or successful disk recovery.
Server tests and source show same-key replay/atomic posting, not a second operation after operator submits a new key.
No process termination, storage fault injection, API call, database access or runtime operation was performed.
recommendation: Unify both active safe-drop entry points on one owner-keyed RetainedRequest service/owner key (or a shared use-case), preserving each screen’s intended active-day/shift gating. Make durable-save failure visible and decide whether high-risk safe-drop may proceed without confirmed retention; if allowed, give operator a recoverable reconciliation path. Keep persistence versioned, protect local financial data, and never persist PIN/password. Do not silently auto-resend on startup; require explicit same-request reconciliation.

needed: Parameterize same safe-drop request behavior across cashier and Control Center; verify identical request ID/payload on same-process retry.
Save an unknown result to the real isolated file-store fixture, reconstruct AppSession and each VM, and verify one replay with identical request ID; assert one server movement/journal/audit.
Inject local Save failure before dispatch and verify the chosen owner-approved behavior: block dispatch or surface an explicit non-durable recovery warning.
Verify cancel/edit/navigation restrictions while pending, plus distinct fresh requests after definitive resolution.
Verify Control Center active-day/new-request and open-shift gates without blocking replay recovery for a previously committed request.
tests.limitations: Only source/tests were reviewed; no test execution or runtime storage fault injection.

source_references.evidence: Cashier Operations safe-drop holds `_pendingSafeDrop` and `_SafeDropRequestId` only as view-model fields; unknown response blocks cancel/edit and retries the same request during the same process, but constructor/restart does not restore it.

Control Center safe-drop uses owner key `controlcenter.safe-drop`, rehydrates pending DTO in the constructor path, and retries through RetainedRequest. It additionally requires active business day and open shift before a new request; a recovered request is retried before the new-request shift gate.
Constructor restores a retained SafeDropRequest, repopulates displayed amount/reason, shows unresolved status, and registers it with AppSession.
Owner-keyed RetainedRequest loads saved DTO at construction and saves it before send; it clears only on definitive success or a definitive initial failure.

File store writes temp then replaces, but catches persistence exceptions and invokes optional callback. It does not itself make send contingent on successful save; actual app config passes no callback.
AppSession unresolved-operation state used by the cashier path is in memory only.
Application configures FileRetainedRequestStore for cashier station with no onError callback, so persistence failures are silently handled by the optional-callback path while requests still proceed.
Existing uncertain-safe-drop test verifies same-view-model identical retry and blocking edit; it does not recreate the VM/store to verify process restart recovery.

Both client entry points call the same server safe-drop endpoint and handler; server checks same-key replay, amount/reason, actor/shift/permission, open business day, locks drawer balance in transaction, and writes one movement/journal/audit.

limitations: Bounded safe-drop workflow comparison; no claim of repository-wide semantic exhaustiveness.
UI-001 is retained as the canonical finding; related client workflow scope is clarified, not duplicated.
